newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Santer-No intention to interfere in U.K. election.
newsitem.headline: Santer-No intention to interfere in U.K. election.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer had no intention of interfering in Britain's election campaign when he made a controversial speech condemning the rise of Euroscepticism, his spokesman said on Tuesday.
Nikolaus van der Pas told reporters the speech, made in Amsterdam on Monday, was an attempt to fight pessimism and growing anti-EU sentiment across Europe, not just in Britain.
"We regret that it has become a party political and electoral issue. We did not intend it to be," van der Pas said.
Santer appeared to have played into the hands of British Eurosceptics with his speech, attacking what he called "doom merchants" and calling for closer integration.
Britain's embattled Conservative prime minister, John Major, fighting an uphill battle to retain power in elections on May 1, has seized on the remarks as proof of an integrationist EU agenda.
The opposition Labour party, leading in opinion polls and viewed as relatively more friendly to the EU, called Santer's comments ill-judged and unwise.
Van der Pas said the Commission never tried to become involved in national politics but Santer had a responsibility to address issues of concern to Europe.
"It is not our intention to interfere in national elections or campaigns," he said. "We have seen rising scepticism in Europe. The president wanted to speak out on that."
He said Santer did not regret what he had said, only the reaction to it.
